businessProblem: Satyam Computer Services' board proposed on 16 December 2008 to acquire Maytas Properties and Maytas Infra — promoter-family entities — and withdrew within hours under investor pressure. The event raises governance, related-party transaction, financial-statement reliability, and fraud risk concerns. Diagnose root causes and recommend highest-priority action plan.

evidence.finding: Satyam's board proposed acquiring Maytas Properties and Maytas Infra — entities linked to the promoter family — on 16 December 2008
evidence.source: Public reporting December 2008, Wikipedia Satyam scandal, academic case studies

evidence.finding: Investors objected strongly to the proposed related-party acquisition, forcing withdrawal within hours
Board approved the related-party acquisition proposal without adequate independent scrutiny — board oversight failure
evidence.source: Academic fraud case studies, public reporting

evidence.finding: Promoter motivation to acquire personal real-estate assets using company funds is a red flag for financial-statement reliability — reported cash position should be independently verified
evidence.source: Fraud risk framework, academic case studies

evidence.finding: Satyam's reported financials show the company as profitable with cash — these figures have not been independently verified
Promoter control risk — promoter-proposed acquisition for personal benefit signals potential misalignment between promoter and shareholder interests
Related-party transaction attempt without adequate independent approval is a governance and legal compliance red flag under Indian corporate law
Investor confidence severely damaged — Satyam stock fell sharply on announcement of proposed acquisition

clientContext.primaryStakeholder: Independent directors, SEBI, auditors, institutional investors

ownerConstraintProfile.followThroughRisk: CRITICAL — promoter motivation to divert assets signals extreme risk
ownerConstraintProfile.resistanceToChange: HIGH — promoter-controlled governance resistant to independent oversight
ownerConstraintProfile.accountabilityWeakness: CRITICAL — board approved related-party acquisition without scrutiny
